newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares flirt with recovery after recent falls.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares flirt with recovery after recent falls.

text.p: Egyptian share prices flirted with recovery on Monday, when they inched up for the first time in five consecutive trading days.
The all-share index rose 1.02 points to 393.74, the Capital Market Authority (CMA) said in its daily report.
On Sunday the index had recorded its fourth consecutive slip and lowest level since February .
Volume on Monday was 116.8 million pounds ($34.4 million), the CMA said.
"People have started buying after the correction mainly because the prices are becoming more attractive," said broker Dalia Sultan of EFG-Hermes.
Commercial International Bank, which was Sunday's most active share, shone again on Monday by dominating trade with 19 million pounds in turnover. Its share closed up 28.34 at 860, the CMA said.
The second most active share was Paints and Chemical Industries/PACHIN, with 15.87 million worth of shares changing hands. Its share slipped 7.35 to close at 139.81.
"I think it should start picking up again because at this price it's very good," Sultan said.
Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA also put on a brave face, attracting 11.1 million pounds in trade with its share price steady, closing at 80.00 pounds.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills WCFM.CA shares reversed a price slide on Sunday, rising 5.57 to Monday's close of 117.07 in 7.39 million turnover.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 635.08 points from 637.16 points on Sunday but the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose, closing at 265.32 from 263.62.
Out of the 86 shares traded, 37 gained, 25 lost and 24 ended the day unchanged.
